# Agama on QoreChain

> A permissioned private-credit vault on QoreChain's testnet (qorechain-diana) where lenders' KYC and the loan tape
> stay encrypted on chain (ML-KEM-1024, QoreSeal) and every decision, price mark, admin action, bridge attestation and
> transaction is signed post-quantum (ML-DSA-87, verified on chain with QoreChain's pqcVerify precompile). Built for
> Build Before Q-Day, the QoreChain Developer Fest, track Encrypted Apps. Live at https://app.agama.finance/qorechain.

## What it is

- Lenders deposit mock USDC into agUSD, a permissioned ERC-4626 vault. 90% of the capital crosses to Ethereum
  Sepolia over a CCTP V2-format bridge to an asset-backed credit issuer; collections come back and lift the price.
- Each lender's account is a PqAccount: a contract controlled only by its owner's ML-DSA-87 key (the key of its QoreX
  wallet), verified on chain with pqcVerify against pqcKeyStatus. The lender signs a plain-text message in QoreX
  (signArbitrary); a relayer submits it and pays the gas. No EVM window, no grant, no gas for the lender.
- KYC: sealed in the browser with ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 (QoreSeal) to the compliance officer and the auditor; the
  chain stores ciphertext. The officer's decision is an ML-DSA-87 signature over the dossier hash, checked by pqcVerify;
  the decision letter is sealed back to the lender.
- Data room: the loan tape is published on chain as a QoreSeal private batch under a per-membership-epoch key, sealed
  to approved lenders and the auditor in parts of eight. Lenders decrypt it in the browser; anyone can check its
  ciphertext commitment.
- Every transaction Agama's accounts send on QoreChain is a hybrid-signed (secp256k1 + ML-DSA-87) native
  MsgCrossVMCall. No role has an EVM window, and the chain refuses an ECDSA-only transaction from any of them.
  QoreChain's explorer shows each one "quantum-safe, verified on-chain".

## Evidence (latest run, docs/battery/native-lane.md)

- Foundry 200/200 (unit, fuzz, 6 invariants, PqAccount, ML-DSA vectors)
- Protocol battery 42/42 (8 lenders against the production keeper), protocol e2e 30/30
- PqAccount battery 26/26, PqAccount attack checks 7/7
- Browser e2e 7/7 and 9/9 with the official QoreX test double, against the deployed app
- Explorer 12/12 transaction kinds quantum-safe; pq-audit 318/318 transactions hybrid-verified
- Bridge messages rebuilt from calldata and state, without logs: 37/37 byte-identical
- 22 findings from tests and the live keeper, each with its fix: docs/FINDINGS.md

## QoreChain features used

Hybrid ML-DSA-87 transactions; PQC key registration with proof of possession; pqcVerify (0x0a01) and pqcKeyStatus
(0x0a02) from Solidity; KEM registry (MsgRegisterKEMKey); cross-VM calls (MsgCrossVMCall); EVM windows (closed, refusal
tested); smart accounts and spending rules (the keeper's gas tank); the fest's fUSD (MsgConvertCoin). Kits: QoreChain
SDK, QoreSeal, QoreSign, qorechain-pqc, QoreX integrations, Asset Kit (QoreChainHybridHolderGuard, ERC-3643 module),
QoreScan (CBOM, DORA mapping).

## Key files

- README.md: overview, verification steps, addresses
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: contracts, keeper, app, PqAccounts, the native lane and how readers work without EVM logs
- docs/THREAT_MODEL.md: every key, what it can and cannot do, quantum and classical attacks
- docs/PQ_ETHEREUM.md: the Ethereum leg (ML-DSA-44 in Solidity, Merkle WOTS+), measured
- docs/FINDINGS.md: what the tests found and what was done
- contracts/src/account/PqAccount.sol: the post-quantum lender account
- contracts/src/qore/AccessRegistry.sol, AgUSD.sol, DataRoom.sol: registry, vault, data room
- keeper/src/native.ts, chain.ts, provenance.ts, pq-audit.ts: native hybrid writes, log-free readers, provenance, audit
- web/lib/server/relay.ts: the relayer (Vercel)

## Scope

Testnets only; mock USDC; the credit book is simulated. Contract creation is the one EVM transaction left (deployment
only). The guardian (pause only) and the gas-tank authenticator (15 QOR a day) are classical keys, by design and
bounded. Licence Apache-2.0.
